featured_reviews.name: Hero Live
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ A Complete Meal with the Perfect Sweet Ending!
This plate is a true celebration of flavors, from royal Awadhi kebabs to a classic dessert.
The Lucknow Gosht Galawati Kebab is the absolute star — incredibly soft, delicately spiced, and so tender that it melts in your mouth. Each bite reflects authentic Awadhi craftsmanship, rich yet perfectly balanced.
The Kafta (Kofta) Kebab is equally satisfying — juicy, flavorful, and cooked to perfection with a lovely outer crust and a moist, well-seasoned center. Paired with the light sautéed vegetables and the creamy baked cheesy side, the plate feels complete and thoughtfully curated.
To refresh the palate, the Big Cola (600 ml) does its job perfectly — chilled, fizzy, and refreshing.
And then comes the highlight of the ending — the Caramel Custard 🍮
Smooth, silky, and perfectly set, with just the right amount of caramel bitterness balancing the sweetness. It’s light, comforting, and an ideal way to close such a rich meal.
✔️ Authentic Awadhi taste
✔️ Excellent texture & balance
✔️ Well-presented, satisfying portions
✔️ Dessert that truly completes the experience
A meal that feels indulgent yet comforting from start to finish.
Highly recommended for kebab lovers and anyone who enjoys ending their meal on a sweet, classic note. 🌟🔥

I visited Jyran at the Sofitel BKC last Friday (Jan 16) with a group of friends, and it was the perfect start to the weekend. The "Modern Nawabi" ambiance and the stunning metal elephant sculpture in the courtyard set the stage for a truly upscale dining experience.
We started with the Aloo Chaat, which was a delightful explosion of tangy and spicy flavors. For starters, the Veg Aloo was beautifully prepared, but the Chicken Tandoori was the clear standout, perfectly charred, smoky, and incredibly succulent. It is rare to find tandoori chicken that remains this moist while packing such a deep punch of traditional spices.
For the main course, the Veg Dum Biryani was a masterclass in slow-cooked perfection. The aroma upon opening the "dum" seal was divine, with every grain of long-grain basmati rice infused with saffron and aromatic spices.
The service was impeccable despite the Friday night rush, making us feel truly welcomed. If you’re looking for authentic Northwest Frontier cuisine in a luxury setting, Jyran is the place to be. I can’t wait to return with the squad!

featured_reviews.name: Mehul Waskar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Masterclass in Fine Dining
I recently visited Tresind Mumbai for lunch, and it was truly an exceptional experience. If you are looking for a place where food meets artistry, this is it.
We opted for the 10-course Chef’s Special non-veg meal, though they also offer an extensive 14-course option. Both menus are thoughtfully curated with excellent choices for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians.
What sets Tresind apart is the incredible attention to detail:
Art on a Plate: Every single dish served was a visual masterpiece. The presentation is sophisticated and creative, making each course feel like a piece of art.
Knowledgeable Service: The staff is highly professional. Before we began, they carefully checked if we had any food allergies, which added a great layer of comfort.
The Story Behind the Food: I loved that they explained every dish—detailing the ingredients and the cooking techniques used. It really helps you appreciate the complexity of the flavors.
It was a deeply flavorful and immersive experience. If you're in Mumbai and want a world-class fine-dining lunch, Tresind is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

Listen, today I was drinking with my friend; there were three of us initially, but one of them left, leaving just the two of us.

Then he questioned whether I could carry the tissues with me, and when I responded, he said some very rude things. There was also a waiter named Bablu who spoke to us very rudely, using abusive language, even after the payment had been made. This behavior was completely inappropriate. They could have communicated politely, but instead, they treated me very badly. Evidence of this can be verified through the CCTV cameras.

This is my request: please understand this situation and spend your time with your friends appropriately.

featured_reviews.name: Jubin B
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited this place for dinner and tried a few dishes from their Mughlai menu.
We started with the Mutton Turkey Boti, which was recommended by the person taking our order. It was basically mutton kebab coated with red mayo/cream. It was decent, but honestly we were expecting a more authentic Mughlai or Lucknowi Nawab-style flavour. Nowadays adding cream and mayo to everything kind of kills the original richness and taste of such dishes. So for us, this starter didn’t really stand out.

Then we had the Murg Lahori with tandoori roti and butter tandoori roti. This dish was actually very good. The gravy had a rich and authentic flavour. One warning though — if you’re not used to spicy food, this curry can literally make you cry 😄. My wife was continuously drinking water after every bite, but thankfully the taste made up for the spice level.

For dessert, we had the Kaju Katli Ice Cream. This was surprisingly really good. Even though it also had a creamy/malai texture, the flavour worked really well here and it genuinely felt worth the money.
Also, the person who served us was really polite and attentive. The way he was serving felt very warm and caring — almost like how a mother serves food at home, with genuine pyaar se hospitality. That really added to the experience.

Overall, a mixed experience — starter was average for us, but the main course and dessert were enjoyable. Good place if you like rich, spicy Mughlai-style food.

featured_reviews.name: AP JP
featured_reviews.review_text: Lunch at the iconic K Bhagat Tarachand, an eatery that serves some wonderful thali since 1895 in Mumbai.  Their lunch service closes at 3.30 so I took an auto to reach the outlet closest to me in Andheri East, just outside the local train station and ordered myself a KBT Combo, a limited thali priced at 419 including taxes.  The thali had a paneer mixed curry, a mixed vegetable curry, a dal fry, with some jeera rice, with 2 pieces of their legendary desi ghee chapati, with a side of masala chaas / buttermilk, roasted papad and a farsan or starter of the day which was a dahi bhalla.  Initially for a limited quantity thali like this, I felt the price point to be very steep, but the quality of the food overlooked the quantity, needless to say the taste was exceptional.  The dahi bhalla, super soft, tender bhalla soaked and seasoned in sweet curd, is a fabulous start.  The paneer sabzi was nothing short of excellence in terms of spice and flavour and both the dal and the mixed veg sabzi had just the right heat to get through the desi ghee overloaded chapatis that were super soft and extremely wellmade.  The jeera rice was much needed to finish off the subzi and dal and the soft indulgent gulab jamoon was waiting to be savoured.  It was a delectable feast that I enjoyed thoroughly paired with some friendly service.  These people are specialists and the thali that I indulged in has taken 100+ years to perfect.  The masala chaas was a perfect accompaniment with the meal.  If you are looking for value you may not find this place suitable, but if you are looking for quality and exceptional taste, you will appreciate this thali that comes highly recommended.

Given that the area has a significant Gujarati community and is largely dominated by vegetarian options, this restaurant provides a refreshing and much-needed alternative for non-vegetarian diners.

Overall, it is a dependable choice for those looking for good non-vegetarian options in Borivali West, and I would certainly recommend it for a satisfying meal.
